title: Covalent packet repair trades wrong-partner access against multivalent clearance and discarded correct links
status_authority: Actual version-bound scoped internal review governs acceptance. Source reports, mathematical verification and physical acquisition remain separate.
reported_status: accepted_internally_verified for the stated conditional race, time-change, birth-death and rooted-prefix counting arguments. Packet assembly/reset remains a proposal; all rates and reported computational examples are hypothetical, not acquired chemistry.
scientific_scope_status: An all-to-all irreversible matching race among n desired handle pairs gives Pcorrect=product_{j=0}^{n-1}(1+j*beta/k)^(-1), while a uniform bound D*beta on each remaining site's wrong-partner hazard gives Pcorrect>=(1+D*beta/k)^(-n). Independent multivalent rebinding can make perfect-sink clearance exponential in arm count. Ideal whole-prefix reset has E[R]=1+L*(1-p)/p rounds but wastes (1-p)*L*(L-1)/2 successful downstream bonds. Independently rooted b-edge packets reduce within-packet waste, excluding fusion. Equal total catalyst exposure alone gives no repair advantage in the common-rate-scaling model.
